CONFIRMED SOURCE CONFLICT 1, inherited restart semantics: environment/instructions/integration.md:7 requires saved records to survive a 'complete process restart over the same database'; tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:23 and :364 require the one completed process restart, and tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:351/:358 grade survival and subsequent writing from it. tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:16-19 promises to 'Stop the running application server process and relaunch the same application on the same database'; :47 reports 'restart complete: the server was relaunched'. In contrast, the generated helper in tests/test.sh:152-159 sends TERM, waits 50 x 0.1 seconds, then continues whether the old process group is still alive or not. Lines 160-169 launch and record a replacement PID without checking it remains alive; :171-183 accept any answering HTTP process. There is no required old-group termination check, escalation after the bounded wait, or new-PID liveness check. Therefore the helper's completed-restart claim can be false while the scored browser checks see unchanged state in the original process. This is an inherited shared-template conflict, not task-specific drift: task tests/test.sh is byte-identical to rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/test.sh, SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa; restart_mcp.py is also byte-identical, SHA256 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5. The frozen template's tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:80-84 makes the same stronger termination/relaunch claim.

CONFIRMED SOURCE CONFLICT 2, inherited undisclosed file-layout restriction: instruction.md:9 asks for the finished app/source/built frontend in /app; environment/instructions/integration.md:5 says start node /app/server.js and serve /app/public/index.html, with all startup assets inside /app (:9/:11). Neither the brief nor any of its six notes disallows symlinks to other files inside /app. tests/test.sh:72-83 nevertheless rejects every symlink except a path under /app/node_modules whose resolved target is also under /app/node_modules. The case at :81 ('*) exit 0 ;;') rejects even /app/public/index.html -> /app/dist/index.html, although both files remain inside the declared deliverable and the requested public path resolves normally. Because write_zero_reward ran at :60 and no suite is reached, a conforming app can receive zero without browser grading. This restriction is also byte-identical to the frozen template, not introduced by this candidate. A source-level branch trace establishes the rejection; no symlink fixture or Docker execution was performed in this scoped review.

counterexample: False pass (source-traced, not newly executed): a one-process Express app uses an in-memory snippet store, exposes the required UI/health and revisions, and installs process.on('SIGTERM', () => {}) while keeping its listener alive. The canonical helper waits about five seconds, launches a replacement that exits on EADDRINUSE, records its PID, and observes HTTP from the original app. It returns success and restart_mcp.py announces a completed restart. All S22 readbacks and a later write can succeed in the original memory store even though actual process replacement would lose the data. False fail (source-traced, not newly executed): an otherwise fully conforming Express/SQLite app ships /app/public/index.html as a symlink to /app/dist/index.html, with all compiled assets inside /app. The public path serves normally, but tests/test.sh:72-83 exits before launch because the link is outside /app/node_modules, retaining reward zero. Ordinary no-symlink golden success does not refute either witness.
suggested_fix: Resolve these upstream shared-template conflicts without silently editing this task's canonical harness: require bounded old-process-group termination and verified replacement-PID liveness before restart success, and either publicly document the exact symlink policy or provide an approved canonical rule accepting safe in-/app links. Bind new targeted resistant-process and conforming-symlink evidence plus the normal golden flow to the approved replacement candidate.
